Altman X post November 6 2025 "$20 billion" annualized revenue run rate 1.4 trillion commitments explain
TechCrunch Altman says OpenAI has $20B ARR and about $1.4 trillion in data center commitments

sources_considered.why: Reports Altman's defensive answer on the BG2 podcast when asked about $13B revenue versus $1.4T commitments.
Reports Altman's November 6 X post setting out revenue plans and funding options.
Syndicated copy of the TechCrunch piece; the original was used.

receipt.public_excerpt: “First of all, we’re doing well more revenue than that. Second of all, Brad, if you want to sell your shares, I’ll find you a buyer,” Altman said. “I just—enough.

evidence_items.explanation: Asked directly how $13B in revenue squares with $1.4T in commitments, Altman deflected with an offer to find a buyer for the host's shares and said 'enough'. This supports the claim that he did not explain. The podcast aired on or before the article date.

receipt.public_excerpt: “We expect to end this year above $20 billion in annualized revenue run rate and grow to hundreds of billion by 2030. We are looking at commitments of about $1.4 trillion over the next 8 years,” he wrote.

evidence_items.explanation: Five days before the post, Altman set out a funding path in public: revenue growing to hundreds of billions by 2030 against $1.4T in commitments over eight years. This cuts against the claim that he gave no explanation.

receipt.public_excerpt: Altman noted that the company may also pay for its needs the old-fashioned way: selling more equity or taking on more loans.

evidence_items.explanation: Altman also named equity and debt as funding sources, along with new business lines. That is a stated explanation, whatever one thinks of it.

receipt.public_excerpt: He predicted revenue will grow steeply, that ChatGPT will continue to grow, and that OpenAI’s developing consumer device business will take off.

evidence_items.explanation: Even on the podcast, Altman pointed to revenue growth as the answer, though without specifics. This shows the deflection was not a total refusal.

unresolved_gaps: Whether Altman's explanation was adequate or credible is a judgment the evidence cannot settle.
No full podcast transcript was read; the BG2 exchange relies on Fortune's account.
